title: OSHA Excavation Checklist (29 CFR 1926.651)
subtitle: For the competent person's inspection before work, during the shift as needed, and after rain or other hazard-increasing events.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item is a Defect, record it and, where it creates a hazardous condition, remove exposed employees from the area until precautions are in place (1926.651(k)(2)).
Equipment manufacturers' instructions, site rules and other Subpart P sections may add checks.

sections.title: Utilities, surface hazards and adjoining structures
items: Anything at the surface that could endanger employees has been removed or supported
Estimated locations of sewer, telephone, fuel, electric, water and other underground lines determined before the excavation was opened

Utility companies or owners contacted within established or customary local response times, advised of the proposed work and asked to establish the location of their installations before excavation started

Where owners could not respond within 24 hours (or a longer period required by state or local law) or could not establish the exact location, work proceeds with caution and with detection equipment or other acceptable means in use
Exact location confirmed by safe and acceptable means as digging nears the estimated location
Exposed underground installations protected, supported or removed
Shoring, bracing or underpinning in place where buildings, walls or other structures are endangered
No excavation below a foundation or retaining wall footing unless one of the conditions in 1926.651(i)(2)(i)–(iv) is met
Not undermined, or a support system or other protection is provided

sections.title: Access, egress and crossings
items: In trenches 4 feet (1.22 m) or deeper, a stairway, ladder, ramp or other safe egress within 25 feet (7.62 m) of lateral travel for every employee
Structural ramps used only by employees designed by a competent person
Equipment ramps designed by a competent person qualified in structural design and built to that design
Ramp and runway members joined so they cannot shift
Ramp and runway members of uniform thickness
Connecting cleats fixed under the runway or placed so they are not a trip hazard
Ramps used instead of steps have cleats or a non-slip top surface
Walkways provided wherever employees or equipment cross over the excavation
Guardrails on walkways 6 feet (1.8 m) or more above lower levels

sections.title: Traffic, loads, equipment and falling material
items: Employees exposed to public traffic wearing reflectorized or high-visibility vests or garments
Nobody beneath loads handled by lifting or digging equipment
Employees standing away from vehicles being loaded or unloaded
Barricades, hand or mechanical signals, or stop logs in use where operators near the edge lack a clear and direct view of it
Excavated material and equipment 2 feet (.61 m) or more back from the edge, or retaining devices holding them
Loose rock or soil on the face
Face scaled, protective barricades installed, or equivalent protection against falling or rolling material

sections.title: Atmosphere and water
items: Where a hazardous or oxygen-deficient atmosphere could exist, air tested before entry into excavations greater than 4 feet deep
Ventilation or respiratory protection in place where oxygen is below 19.5 percent or the atmosphere is hazardous
Ventilation or other precautions keep exposure from exceeding 20 percent of the lower flammable limit
Atmosphere retested as often as needed while controls are relied on
Breathing apparatus, harness and line, basket stretcher or similar readily available where hazardous atmospheres exist or may develop, and attended when in use
Employees in bell-bottom pier holes or similar deep confined footings wear a harness with a separate, individually attended lifeline
No work in standing or accumulating water unless precautions such as shield systems, water removal or harness and lifeline are in place
A competent person monitors pumps and water removal operations
Diversion ditches, dikes or other means keep surface water out where natural drainage is interrupted
Excavations subject to heavy-rain runoff inspected by a competent person, with (h)(1) and (h)(2) met

sections.title: Competent person inspection
items: Excavation, adjacent areas and protective systems checked for signs of cave-in, protective system failure, hazardous atmospheres and other hazards
Inspection done before work started and repeated as needed during the shift
Re-inspection completed after every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing occurrence
Exposed employees kept out of any area where a hazard was found until precautions are taken

references: 29 CFR 1926.651: Specific excavation requirements (Part 1926 Subpart P: Excavations)
